text:
ana: Heads-up — product wants trace-derived SLOs for generation latency (p95 <= 250ms) and an error budget tied to span status. Need recommendations on retention, sampling, and exporter choices.

mike: +1. Are we doing full-trace retention for 30d? that's expensive. maybe retain aggregated histograms and sampled raw spans.

jess: For SLOs we actually only need counts of "good" vs "bad" traces plus percentile approximations. We can use aggregate exports (histogram buckets) for 30d and keep full traces for 7d.

ram: Question: how do we define "bad"? do we treat 5xx and generation timeout as errors? do partial responses count?

ana: product wants: any span with status != OK OR generation_duration > 250ms counts as error. partial responses only if final status is ERROR.

mike: That means we need span attributes forwarded to exporter: status.code, http.status_code, generation.ms. OTLP includes attributes fine. But sampling matters — if we drop too many spans we lose denominator.

jess: Proposal: 1) front-door sample rate 1% full traces, 2) deterministic tail-sampling for traces with errors/high-latency to keep those, 3) export pre-aggregated histograms (per-route) at 1m intervals to metrics storage for 90d retention.

ram: Tail-sampling rules? Can we implement in the collector? e.g., keep traces where any span.attr generation.ms > 200 OR status.code != 0

ana: Yes, use Collector tail-sampling processor. Example config snippet we tested: 
```yaml
processors:
  tailsampling:
    policies:
      - name: high_latency_or_error
        type: probabilistic
        sample_rate: 1
        decision_wait: 30s
        match:
          - attributes:
              - key: generation.ms
                value: ">200"
              - key: status.code
                value: "!=0"
```

mike: Nice. On exporter choice — OTLP to Tempo + metrics exporter to Prometheus/Grafana Cloud for histograms. We should also provide a lightweight OTLP->S3 dump for raw traces if customer wants long-term.

jess: For SLO calculation in Grafana we can expose two derived metrics: slo_good_count and slo_total_count. Query (pseudo): 
```promql
good = sum(rate(slo_good_count[5m]))
total = sum(rate(slo_total_count[5m]))
error_budget = 1 - (good/total)
```
Then compute burn rate and alerting on error budget windows.

ram: How do we compute slo_good_count from traces? Use TraceQL/Tempo or exporter to generate metric at ingestion: 
- increment slo_total_count per trace
- if duration <= 250ms and status == OK increment slo_good_count

ana: That logic can live in collector or in a lightweight trace-to-metric pipeline (we already have a small service). Advantage: metrics are cheap and support 90d retention at scale.

mike: UX question for Console: product wants a per-route SLO widget with breakdown by percentile buckets and an error budget gauge and a timeline of burn. We need consistent labels: route, model_version, region. These must be emitted as attributes on root span.

jess: Also add rollouts UX: when model version flips, we need to show SLOs for both candidate and baseline and an automatic fallback if error_budget crosses threshold. That ties into routing policy service.

ram: On quotas/billing: we need to ensure sampled traces don't undercount usage for billing. Billing should rely on request logs not trace sample counts. Add note.

ana: Telemetry-bot: created ticket PLAT-4123 to implement tail-sampling policy + trace->metric exporter. ETA next sprint. :white_check_mark:

telemetry-bot: PLAT-4123: Added collector config proposal, sample retention plan: raw traces 7d, aggregated histograms 90d, raw exports to S3 on-demand.

mike: Performance question: if we generate metrics per-trace in collector we may blow up cardinality. Limit labels to route/model_version/region only (no user ids). Also bucket durations to avoid high-card.

jess: Suggested histogram buckets: [0,50,100,150,200,250,300,500,1000,2000]ms. That gives decent percentile resolution around SLO.

ram: For alerting thresholds: alert when 10m burn rate > 2 OR 1h error_budget usage > 80%. We should add preflight notifications on rollouts.

ana: Implementation plan summary: 
- push collector tailsampling rules + attribute enrichment
- export histograms to metrics backend with 90d retention
- keep full traces 7d, plus on-demand S3 export for 180d if needed
- implement trace->metric transformer to emit slo_good_count/slo_total_count
- Console: per-route SLO panel + percentiles + burn gauge + rollout diff view

mike: Sounds good. Can one of you own Console pieces? I'll take collector and export plumbing.

jess: I'll own trace->metric transformer and the Grafana dashboard templates.

ram: I'll do the rollout UX hooks and coordinate with routing team for model_version labels.

sre-oncall: Please add runbook entries for degraded telemetry — if collector CPU spikes we fallback to 1% sample and switch to metrics-only SLOs.

ana: cool. I'll update PLAT-4123 with owners, config snippets, and a short cost estimate. We'll sync in next standup.

telemetry-bot: Reminder: RFC window opens tomorrow for 3 days for feedback on retention/cost tradeoffs.

ana: thanks everyone :pray:
